skills.trigger: When evaluating a focal lung opacity on chest radiography to distinguish between alveolar consolidation and other patterns like ground-glass, nodules, or interstitial disease.
steps: Inspect the density and internal architecture of the opacity: look for homogeneous increased attenuation that obscures underlying vascular markings (silhouette sign) combined with visible dark branching tubular structures (air bronchograms).

Differentiate from alternatives: Ground-glass opacities appear hazy with preserved vessels; nodules are discrete round densities; interstitial patterns show reticular/linear networks; calcifications appear markedly dense/bone-like. The presence of air bronchograms within a dense opacity specifically confirms alveolar filling (consolidation).
